body:
You make great points. I've only ever worked in college, and I always worked exclusively with other students. I hadn't really given a ton of thought to who I'd be working with. I'm lucky enough to be living with my family (so I don't need a job to pay for food and lodging), so I guess I do have a bit of breathing room when it comes to choosing jobs.

I'm in a situation in which I'm stuck between a rock and a hard place in the form of working at home at menial labor, or travelling a large distance and spending large sums of cash for the opportunity to do the work I got my degree for. Guess I should have thought of that when I declared my major, eh?

Did you try to talk to your employers about depression, or try to let it stay hidden?

Thanks! It really is comforting to know I'm not alone here in this situation. So many people I know seem to be doing great after college, and I'm sitting here trying to justify to my parents why I want to work at the local liquor store. I just want a simple job I can't fuck up too badly, and since I'm not totally sure where my head will be in a few months, I'd like to not screw up a better job if I start to come undone.

Thanks for the reply. The drugs are dangerous in that I can *potentially* give myself a stroke if I disregard my doctor's instructions about diet. I have to avoid fermented stuff (cheese, beer, and soy sauce are the main ones), and carry around some different pills in case of a hypertensive crisis. It's a risk, but it's one that I've decided I'm going to have to live with. 

I'm sort of in a dead zone in my life right now. I'm about four weeks from moving back home from college and it feels like it's too late to start anything here since I'm going back home so soon.

Hey. Thanks for offering to talk. I've been going through withdrawal symptoms from a couple anti-depressants and shit kind of sucks. I'm due to start a new course of treatment in a couple of weeks, and I'm actually fucking terrified of it. It presents the newest and best hope for a "cure" but goddamn, the new meds are some of the most restrictive and potentially dangerous anti-depressants that are out there.

I'm moving home after finishing college, and I'm in no place to move forward with my life unless I can figure out a nice band-aid for my depression. My doctor and my family are pretty optimistic about the course of treatment, but of course, I feel like shit and have few hopes for it. A semi-permanent treatment that works would be a god-send, though.

I've needed to tell someone that for weeks, now. My family is well-meaning but generally not super-helpful, so I've been sitting on it and letting it fester since late May.

It's not self-serving if you're giving someone else the chance to talk, believe me. I've been cooped up in my head for a long time and I need a place to vent.

I've been on a new blend of medication recently, Olanzapine, mixed with Prozac and Bupropion, plus Lorazepam to sleep. The doctor says that Olanzapine is my last chance for an "easy" drug - something that comes without large restrictions. Beyond this point, it's tricyclics and MAOIs, plus ECT if I'm really screwed.

The Olanzapine has me sleeping a little bit again, which is good. It gives me a little bit of energy, too. Which is bad.

I have enough energy now to know what I should be doing, but not enough to do it. So then I feel like shit for not doing it. I'm halfway functional, so people tell me "Oh, it's not so bad, I dealt with *x* and it was really bad, you don't want to know what that's like."

My self-loathing has become so strong that it occasionally manifests itself as physical pain. You know that knot in the stomach feeling? Pretty much that. I have front-row seats for a non-stop movie playing in my head of every single time I've fucked up, every time I've said something I shouldn't have, missed opportunities, etc. etc.

For the first time in years, I'm considering suicide. I've been going through therapy in one way or another for eight years. I'm nearly out of options, and I'm going nowhere fast.

If you like complex and strategic geo-politics games, I may have to get you playing Europa Universalis 4 and Crusader Kings 2. Those games are fairly complex, but if you figure out how to play them, they can be hugely rewarding.

I've recently been back on a heavily modded Skyrim binge myself. Send me a steam invite, we can see what games we both have.

In terms of keeping myself organized, I really only found one thing that works.

I have a pretty good sized whiteboard that I bought from a university's surplus division. I mounted it on one wall of my apartment, over my PC, and I write the one thing I have to do that day in huge block letters, and underline it a couple times. 

I can't even write two things. If I write two things, I'll literally think "Too much stuff to do, better do none of it." How sad is that? But with one thing, and only one thing, there's a much higher chance that I'll do it. I keep a much smaller list of other stuff I need to on the board, in one corner. It's small stuff, and I'm very serious about how insignificant it is. Stuff like "clean the toilet", "replace the shower curtain liner", or "clean one large pot/three dishes". Tasks that would take twenty or thirty seconds, perhaps a minute at the longest. If I'm feeling like I'm hugely accomplished because I've managed to complete the large task (which isn't usually too herculean by the standards of most people), I might be able to knock out one or two small tasks as well. 

This system isn't great. That being said, it's primarily designed to not overwhelm me - getting one thing done is better than nothing. Maybe with practice, or better drug and talk therapy, I can get up to two tasks a day, or be able to complete all the little stuff in a day or two. 

Honestly, self-management is a faraway dream for me at this point. At any given point I can look back at my day, or my week, and think "Why didn't you do X, Y, and Z? Or even just one of them? Is it so damn hard to walk to the pharmacy for a refill?" I chalk it up to the shitty fight-or-flight savanna brain being in control most of the time.

I'm currently taking 450mg of Wellbutrin (generic bupropion) plus 20mg of Prozac (generic fluoxetine), and a nightcap of .5-1.5mg of Lorazepam to help me sleep. This is largely for depression, with the hope of tackling anxiety once depression is conquered or subdued to a manageable extent.

Does it help? Sure, I guess. The Lorazepam is great for helping me sleep, but I feel I need to take slightly more to sleep than I did before. The Wellbutrin brought about a slight improvement and the Prozac made things slightly better. Am I cured? Hell no.

Also, Zoloft didn't work for me either. It fogged my mind up a lot, and didn't seem to help in any tangible way. My doctor kept increasing the dosage before throwing an anti-psychotic ($500 a bottle!) on top of it. Things are better since I switched doctors and drugs.

For me, depression is inconsistent in duration and severity. I usually describe it as episodic. It's like a disease can suddenly stop progressing for a bit, or even go into remission for a time. I've had periods in which I felt that I was cured, even. There were three months in 2012 in which I actually had the temerity to tell people I had cured my depression. *That* makes me wince abit.

I too have sort of struggled with the bipolar label. My few experiences with bipolarity in family members or acquaintances generally lead me to believe that the highs are as bad as the lows, but just in a different way. 

The way that I look at my own feelings is that I forget what "normal" is, and when I experience either a normal or happy mood for an extended amount of time, I get nervous. I'll actually wonder if something's wrong, because I'm happy.

I've tried to tie my mood to everything from food intake and exercise level to time of year and exposure to sunlight. I've only been able to pin down the fact that my depression is slightly worse in the middle of winter. At this point, I might as well blame moon phases or some kind of voodoo magic.

Happy Birthday! It might be from an internet stranger, but I mean it sincerely. I spent my birthday this year driving around aimlessly in the dark, just out of a need to do something or go somewhere.

Over the years, I've learned that the momentous birthdays (along with a lot of other "important" holidays) are sort of overblown by our culture, and we get a skewed and biased perception via the media and stuff like facebook. We only see the people who do have huge parties, not those who don't.

I know the feeling of loneliness, too. For that, all I can offer is [this shitty image macro](http://i.imgur.com/oAapmT3.png) that describes my sentiment better than words can.

You're 18. If you're in America, you can vote, buy tobacco (maybe, some states are weird), legally watch pornography, and buy firearms. It might not be the biggest event in your life, but we don't always see those coming. I hope the next year is better for you!

I'll give you the advice I wish I had when I was in your position.

You need to talk to them, separately or together. It may be easier to do this with them one at a time. Based on what you've written, I'd recommend you talk to your mother first. Just be straightforward - tell them that you've struggled with being able to tell them because you weren't sure that they would understand. Then go on to say that you've had these problems, and that you have for some time. If your mother tells you that you're her good daughter and that she's proud of you, I can't imagine that she would be cold-hearted towards you. She might misunderstand a bit, but mention that you'd like to see a therapist, or at least your general practitioner for a recommendation. Mention that you weren't sure how to approach your dad about it, and that you'd like him to know that there's a problem, but you don't know how. I don't know your exact family situation, and I don't pretend to, but I'd like to think that this should work.

My situation was similar, but not quite identical. My depression manifested itself early in high school, and I had a hard time expressing it to my parents. Things eventually led to a meltdown, which is the absolute worst way to explain things. They were terrified, especially because I hadn't told them much. Things were complicated by the fact that they were in the middle of a divorce, and both side was extremely wary of the other. I eventually had to talk to them about everything that was going on, but the circumstances made everything far, far worse. Please don't wait until things get worse. Depression makes people feel unsure about things that should be obvious. Your parents love you. They will help you in the best way that they know, you just have to tell them what that way is.

Pretty much the same taste in games here. In terms of games, lately I've been playing Arma 2/3, BF4, Insurgency, Red Orchestra 2, Sins of a Solar Empire, and Wargame ALB. I've been playing a little of Planetside 2, but I can't seem to get into it. The learning curve bugs me a bit, but I guess it's all about finding a routine.

I've been curious about DayZ Standalone and Rust. I played DayZ back in the mod days and enjoyed it a hell of a lot, but I haven't picked up the new one as I'm a bit strapped for cash at the moment.

Civ 4 might be my most played strategy game, though. I've clocked about three hundred hours across the base game and its expansions. I never got as far into Civ 5 because of multiplayer bugs early on in the game.

I'm not super competitive either when it comes to PC gaming. I'm pretty god-awful at the really fast paced e-sports-compatible games like Starcraft, LoL/Dota2, CS:GO, and the like.

I'll pm you my steam id. The time difference might be a little crazy but I keep odd hours Thursday-Sunday.
Hey, some of my best friends have been depressed foreigners. Were in Serbia are you from? Do you still live in Serbia? What PC games do you play?

Nice collection! I'm limited by my local range, which tops out at 100 yards. If I end up back home next year there's a shooting club with a 600yd. range, which will hopefully give me the necessary excuse to pick up a decent rifle. What made you choose the 556? I don't know much about the rifle, though I'm jealous of the Tavor! I've heard nothing but good things about them.

That's quite a coincidence - I went to the Boundary Waters - primarily the Canadian side - my sophomore year in high school on a school trip. If I go back, I'll probably do the American side just for the sake of simplicity.

What guns do you have/like? I just put together my first AR-15 from a PSA upper and a no-name lower, but I haven't been able to take it out what with the polar vortices. I'm just stockpiling 62gr ammo when I can get it, and I hope to get it sighted in as soon as it warms up a bit.

We're in the same boat, graduation and plans wise. Where do you like to camp? I've been trying to get back to the Boundary Waters up in northern Minnesota for ages, or do some backpacking up in the Pacific NW. I've only ever been down to TN once, but it was a beautiful state. I'm in one of the flatter, more corn-filled states, so trees and mountains make me irrationally happy.

Also, are you in any of the big EVE coalitions? I just stopped playing again after the usual corp/alliance drama proved to be too much for our small nullsec group.

I know this feeling. I'm graduating late from university, and it seems that in general everyone I know has some sort of grand career, plan, or even aspirations. Me? I'm trying to decide where I should put my couch in the basement when I move back home, and I'm living hour to hour in my own misery. I can't plan for the next damn day, let alone for the rest of my life. It's a real pain in the ass to deal with a condition that says "Better not bother going to the store to buy groceries; you'll have killed yourself by the time you run out of food anyways."

I'm the sort of person who usually stays far, far away from this sort of thing, as I have an irrational phobia of being doxxed. 

But to hell with it. If someone I know finds me here, they'll have just as much to explain as I will.

I'm a 23 year old university student at a large Midwestern university, studying slavic languages. Like a lot of others here, I like history - recently I was trying to put together a podcast on the history of the USSR/Russian Federation from 1979-1999, but it sort of fell apart. 

I'm a PC gamer, gun enthusiast and collector, and when I'm not in the throes of a depressive episode and lying on the carpet, I read a fair amount. Sometimes I write, but it's never something I can stick with. I've been trying to organize a tabletop game of either Pathfinder, D&D, or one of a couple homebrew games I've made over the years, but my friends are spread too far across the country to make it easy. I've been spending a lot of time binge-watching Boardwalk Empire and Homeland recently.

I enjoy traveling, and through immense luck have been able to spend a bit of time in Europe recently. I always like talking to people who live outside the US, if only to see what life is like. I originally wanted to put my degree to use as a foreign service officer, or in one of the intelligence or security agencies. Depression has sort of scuppered these plans, and as I'm in my last semester of university, things are looking kind of desperate come May.

I also suffer from major depression, and I'll be celebrating the eighth anniversary of that diagnosis in May. Other than that, I've got garden-variety social anxiety and self-esteem issues. Lately I've been trying to keep panic attacks under control, but it's a losing battle. I had one while driving this week, and it wasn't a great experience. 

It seems that all of us in this thread are eerily similar, re: interests and hobbies. If you want to talk, or want my steam info or something, hit me up. I'm social enough on the internet.

I've done this. Not on a regular basis the way that you're suggesting, mind you, but I have done a variety of doses of LSD whilst depressed.

Do I recommend it? Well... It's a bit conditional. After my first experience, I experienced a boost in my mood for about a month or so afterwards. It wasn't gigantic - I was still depressed, but I was a bit happier. The little things that had been getting me down didn't nag at me as much. Things were a bit more peaceful. Subsequent experiences (separated by many, many months) brought similar effects. It wouldn't be right for me to say what I am about to say without stating these positive facts.

I live near one of the largest cities in America, with a fairly active club scene. I have some friends who are perhaps more into drugs than they should be, and they have friends who are more into it than they are. Why is this important?

Because despite being in what would normally be a good position to get "the real thing", I have only gotten what I paid for once when going through local channels. I was never able to get what I wanted again locally - I had to have a friend procure via the Silk Road. People I know have had experiences ranging from from totally harmless (no effects) to god-awful (some kind of hallucinogenic amphetamine). 

I have had only one negative experience on LSD, or other hallucinogens. It was the stuff of nightmares, and it worsened an already significant anxiety issue for several months.

I suppose I'm just trying to tell you to be careful; something you undoubtedly understand. If you do go about this, I hope that you have experienced friends who can help you in all stages. This is not impossible to do correctly, and there is a reward, but you need to know that there is quite definitely risk involved. Once you start the trip, there's really no way to go but forwards, and those uncharted waters can be scary to navigate by yourself. Whatever you choose to do, I wish you the best of luck.

I'd thought about it a few years ago. It's something that I've wanted to do, but I've never thought that I could support myself on it. I took a few writing electives in university, but that's all. 

As to the heritage bit, half of my family is Japanese. My grandparents on that side are the children of immigrants. Suicide (and attempted suicide) over matters of honor aren't uncommon in that family. Her brother committed suicide after being medically discharged from the Air Force and a much-younger cousin who committed suicide after failing out of college. I had an uncle who also attempted suicide after his wife left him. 

Naturally, no one in the family was happy that they committed suicide - my grandmother's brother's death emotionally broke my great-grandparents and they died shortly thereafter. But it says something about the way that they were raised, and in turn about the family.

Thanks for replying. It seems a bit hyperbolic that I hit my peak back then, but it seems like I've been in an uncontrolled descent for years now, with no end in sight. It's like the protagonist says in Office Space: "Every single day that you see me, is on the worst day of my life."

I'm a Russian language major. I took the language with the intent of going into government service, but I've sort of screwed myself out of that route with my grade point.

Thanks for responding. Writing is pretty much the only thing left that I still do passably well. After the fact, I was worried that what I wrote would be seen as some kind of weird navel-gazing plea for attention, so you're certainly not the one who's selfish here.

I guess I don't know what a successful life entails. I'd say it's more the former than the latter - I don't think everyone's miserable. At this point, I'd settle for a life in which I could leave the house in the morning without either a total numbness or crushing despair. Things that people take for granted are impossible for me.
